A just energy transition is not simply a technological shift. It is a development strategy. — it is social policy, industrial policy, climate policy, and a development priority all at once. 

This week, I’m with @UNDP colleagues in Dakar, Senegal, alongside 20+ country offices, energy experts, financiers and development practitioners to focus on what matters most: turning clean energy into development outcomes. 

Africa holds the world’s greatest renewable potential — including 60% of global high-quality solar and nearly 8,000 GW of solar capacity — and 30% of critical mineral reserves, positioning the continent to lead the green industrial economy.

How can we re-think Africa’s economic transformation through a just energy transition? 

Three opportunities will define its transition:
 
1️⃣ First, Africa is becoming central to the global clean-energy economy, building on green industry. Africa can go behind producing clean power — it can also industrialize it, from agro-processing to e-mobility to mineral value chains. A transformation that could save 3.7 million lives every year. 

2️⃣  Second, de-risking is essential to unlock finance at scale. Africa needs USD 190–200 billion annually for energy investment, yet risk is perceived at 2–3× reality. Blended finance, guarantees, and policy reform can flip this equation and turn pipelines into projects. 

3️⃣  Third, digitalization and AI make this transformation even more powerful, as scaling energy access is an economic imperative, which can reduce technical and commercial losses by up to 20-30%. Access must move from pilots to performance — especially for clean cooking and for deploying digital innovations that boost efficiency and productive use.

#Digital and #AI tools can lower costs, improve planning, and support de-risking — but they are enablers, not substitutes. Community engagement, local capacity, and strong institutions remain the backbone of a just energy transition, especially where digital ecosystems are still emerging. 

Energy is ultimately about people, jobs, and dignity. This week in Dakar, with UNDP colleagues and partners across Africa, we are working to turn the continent’s renewable wealth into universal access, green industries, and inclusive growth.

#EnergyForDevelopment
